title: Phenomenology of Spirit
author: G.W.F. Hegel
desc: Obra cumbre del idealismo alemán. La dialéctica del amo y el esclavo, fundamento que Marx invirtió para el materialismo histórico.
tesis: La Fenomenología del Espíritu de Hegel es la montaña que Marx escaló para ver más lejos. La dialéctica del amo y el esclavo — donde el esclavo, al trabajar, desarrolla conciencia mientras el amo se estanca — es el germen de toda la filosofía de la liberación. Marx 'puso a Hegel de pie': la dialéctica no es del Espíritu sino de la materia, no de la Idea sino de la lucha de clases. Para entender a Marx hay que entender qué invirtió.
ideas: La dialéctica del amo y el esclavo es el germen de la filosofía de la liberación: el oprimido desarrolla conciencia a través del trabajo.
Hegel descubrió la dialéctica — Marx la puso 'de pie': de idealismo a materialismo.
La Fenomenología es el texto más difícil de la filosofía occidental pero su estructura dialéctica es la base de todo el marxismo.
contexto: Publicada en 1807 cuando Hegel tenía 36 años. Terminó el manuscrito la noche antes de la batalla de Jena, donde Napoleón derrotó a Prusia. Hegel vio a Napoleón pasar a caballo y escribió que había visto 'el Espíritu del mundo'. Es el texto filosófico más influyente del siglo XIX y la montaña que Marx tuvo que escalar.

conexiones.razon: Engels explica cómo Marx superó a Hegel pasando del idealismo al materialismo.
Los Manuscritos de 1844 son la primera inversión materialista de Hegel.
Dussel va más allá de Marx: no solo invierte a Hegel sino que lo desborda con la exterioridad del Otro.

p. iv
Revolución Francesa derroca al régimen feudal

there was the French Revolution of 1789 which had upended all conventional thought in Europe. While at Tübingen, Schelling, Hegel, and Hölderlin had in fact all been excited by the prospects in France.
p. xi
Libertad absoluta y Terror jacobino
It is therefore the coldest, emptiest death of all, having no more meaning than chopping off a head of cabbage or swallowing a mouthful of water.
Hegel se gradúa en el Seminario de Tubinga

When he graduated from Tübingen’s famous Theological Seminary in 1793, his career path had supposedly already been set for him. He was supposed, and in one sense even obligated, to become a Lutheran pastor in the duchy of Württemberg.
p. x
Hegel llega a Jena como Privatdozent
Schelling managed to arrange for Hegel to leave Frankfurt and come to Jena in 1801, where, at the age of thirty-one, Hegel decided to see if he could make his mark as a philosopher.
p. x
Termina la Fenomenología bajo el cañón de Jena

It was in fact at Jena on October 14 that the decisive battle took place, and Napoleon and his army delivered a crippling blow to the Prussian army... Hegel was later to claim that he finished the writing of the book under the sound of the cannon fire of the battle itself.
p. xi
Lee la Fenomenología del Espíritu de Hegel
The following is an advertisement for the Phenomenology which was run originally in the Bamberger Zeitung in July 1807 and was almost certainly written by Hegel himself.
La verdad es el todo: tesis del Prólogo

That the true is only actual as a system, or, that substance is essentially subject, is expressed in the representation that expresses the absolute as spirit – the most sublime concept and the one which belongs to modernity and its religion.
El espíritu del mundo carga con la historia

Both because the substance of the individual, the world spirit, has possessed the patience to pass through these forms over a long stretch of time and to take upon itself the prodigious labor of world history.
Dialéctica del amo y el siervo

The relation of both self-consciousnesses is thus determined in such a way that it is through a life and death struggle that each proves its worth to itself... The former is the master, the latter is the servant.
El miedo a la muerte, el amo absoluto
It felt the fear of death, the absolute master. In that feeling, it had inwardly fallen into dissolution, trembled in its depths, and all that was fixed within it had been shaken loose.
Antígona y la ley no escrita
That way they count for Sophocles’ Antigone as the unwritten and unerring law of the gods: Not now and yesterday, but forever / It lives, and nobody knows from whence it appeared.
El Gólgota del espíritu absoluto
they form the recollection and the Golgotha of absolute spirit, the actuality, the truth, the certainty of its throne, without which it would be lifeless and alone.
